text:
Sandis Vilmanis lasted 2.1 minutes in Washington on Nov 7. Tom Wilson boarded him, was ejected, and wasn't suspended, which Florida Hockey Now called wrong; RMNB headlined Wilson's explanation as "I was trying to make a north-south hit". Vilmanis missed time, came back against Detroit on Nov 12, as The Hockey News reported, and set up a goal against St. Louis two nights later.

The bigger story is that a 2022 fifth-round pick has become a useful Panther. He has 8 points in 18 games, including a 2-goal, 2-assist night against Chicago on Nov 4, on under 13 minutes a night. None of it looks like luck: his 3 goals match his chances, and at five on five Florida has had 59.4% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, 9 points better than without him. He also has 54 hits. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, from only 6 games last season, had him getting to the front of the net often and taking 55% of his shots off the rush. At 22, with 37 NHL games behind him, our range has him at 25 to 44 points by season's end.
headline: Vilmanis is back from the Wilson hit and producing
